title: To amend title 5, United States Code, to authorize the increase of the retirement age in the United States Capitol Police.
official_title: To amend title 5, United States Code, to authorize the increase of the retirement age in the United States Capitol Police.
summary: Capitol Police officers currently face mandatory retirement at age 60. This bill replaces that fixed age with a range, letting the Capitol Police Board set the mandatory retirement age at any point between 57 and 65 — giving it more flexibility to retain experienced officers beyond the current 60-year cap.
brief: Raises the Capitol Police Board's maximum retirement age waiver from 60 to 65, letting the Board keep experienced officers working longer.

top_lines.headline: Retirement Age Flexibility
subs: Capitol Police Board can now set mandatory retirement at any age between 57 and 65 — replacing the current fixed age of 60
Applies to officers under both the Civil Service Retirement System and the Federal Employees' Retirement System

likelihoodReason: Bipartisan support (Steil R-WI and Morelle D-NY) on a narrow workforce management bill affecting a single law enforcement agency. Capitol security legislation typically advances with little controversy. The limited scope and lack of broader policy implications make Senate passage plausible if floor time is available.

items.main: Amends Sections 8335(c) and 8425(c) of title 5, United States Code to expand the Capitol Police Board's authority over mandatory retirement age from a fixed ceiling of 60 to a range of 57 to 65.
items.detail: Both the Civil Service Retirement System (Section 8335(c)) and Federal Employees' Retirement System (Section 8425(c)) provisions are amended by replacing "becomes 60 years of age" with "attains an age determined by the Board that shall be not less than 57 years of age and not more than 65 years of age." Prior law fixed mandatory retirement at age 60; under the amended text the Board sets a mandatory retirement age anywhere within the 57–65 range for individual officers or as a general policy.

gaps: The bill grants the Board discretion to set retirement age between 57 and 65 but specifies no criteria the Board must use in making that determination for individual officers or as a department-wide policy.

modified: Section 8335(c) of title 5, United States Code (CSRS) — Capitol Police mandatory retirement age ceiling raised from 60 to 65, at the Board's discretion
Section 8425(c) of title 5, United States Code (FERS) — Capitol Police mandatory retirement age ceiling raised from 60 to 65, at the Board's discretion
